text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
IgaSwiat(athlete) ::: athlete is Iga Świątek.
RafaelNadal(athlete) ::: athlete is Rafael Nadal.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
RolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are one of the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaSwiat) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly.
∀x (FemalePlayer(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x) → LostTo(x, IgaSwiat)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (RolandGarros2022(x) → (FemalePlayer(x) ∨ MalePlayer(x))) ::: All tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros in 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
∀x ((CocoGauff(x) ∧ (RankedHighly(x) ∨ LostTo(x, RafaelNadal))) → ¬MalePlayer(x)) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
CocoGauff(coco) ∧ RolandGarros2022(coco) ::: Coco Gauff is at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
∀x (CocoGauff(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: Coco Gauff is among the most active major tennis players.
